name: Maastricht Aachen Airport
before:
A cargo airport with a passenger service attached, at Beek in Limburg, 9 km north east of Maastricht and 28 km north west of Aachen just over the German border. It is second in the Netherlands for freight, handling 29,448 tonnes in 2024 against 230,932 passengers.

Ground transport is straightforward. Arriva bus line 30 runs every thirty minutes to Maastricht and Sittard, connecting with the national rail network at both stations. The airport sits on the A2 at exit 50, there are two car parks and several hire firms, and a GR8 hotel opened 50 metres from the terminal in 2021.

One useful option for a client whose flight does not work: KLM runs a bus to Schiphol by way of Maastricht station and Eindhoven Airport, sold as an add-on to a KLM ticket.

There is a good deal of aviation industry here too, including an aircraft painting facility running since the late 1980s, a maintenance operation, and the EUROCONTROL upper area control centre.
after:
A cargo airport with a passenger service attached, 9 km north east of Maastricht and 28 km north west of Aachen, just over the German border. On Eurostat's figures it was second in the Netherlands for freight in 2025, handling about 41,600 tonnes against about 156,000 passengers.

Ground transport is straightforward. Arriva bus line 30 between Maastricht and Sittard stops in front of the terminal and calls at the railway stations of Maastricht, Sittard and Beek-Elsloo. Hertz, Sixt and Europcar hire cars here. There is also a Gr8 hotel at the airport.
